study_identification.title: Analyzing heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease using multimodal normative modeling on imaging-based ATN biomarkers

study_characteristics.study_objective: This study aimed to identify individual patterns of neuroanatomical and neuropathological variation in the brains of individuals with Alzheimer disease (AD) using a deep learning-based normative modeling framework across amyloid-tau-neurodegeneration (ATN) imaging biomarker data. The objectives were to: (i) assess the extent of neuroanatomical and neuropathological variability between individual patients based on overlapping or distinct patterns of abnormal deviations, (ii) quantify intra-group heterogeneity within AD spectrum clinical groups, (iii) estimate a disease severity index (DSI) for each individual that captures both spatial extent and magnitude of regional abnormal deviations across ATN, and (iv) examine whether DSI is related to severity of dementia, impaired cognition, and risk of disease progression.

dataset_name.answer: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative); Knight ADRC (Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Washington University in St. Louis)

hc_age.answer: ADNI-CU: mean 71.5, SD 7.2; ADRC-CU: mean 68.2, SD 7.3

imaging_modality.answer: T1-weighted MRI; Amyloid PET (18F-Florbetapir); Tau PET (18F-Flortaucipir)

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer v6.0 (ADNI); FreeSurfer v5.3 (ADRC); Desikan-Killiany atlas (66 cortical ROIs); Aseg atlas (24 subcortical ROIs); PET Unified Pipeline (PUP) for ADRC PET processing; ICV normalization for ROI volumes

quality_checking_detail.answer: For Knight ADRC: All images failing quality control check were reprocessed to ensure consistency across scans. MRI preprocessing included visual quality control with reprocessing when necessary. No specific quantitative metrics or exclusion numbers are provided in the main text or supplementary materials.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Transfer learning approach: mmVAE model was first trained on ADNI-CU-train dataset (n=326), then fine-tuned on ADRC-CU-tl dataset (n=225) to address dataset-specific biases and domain shifts. The model was conditioned on age and sex to remove covariate effects. Fine-tuning was used to adapt the pre-trained normative model to the replication cohort, addressing differences in scanners (different MRI scanners between ADNI and ADRC), FreeSurfer versions (v6.0 for ADNI vs v5.3 for ADRC), and recruitment strategies. Authors acknowledge that harmonization methods such as ComBat could further mitigate scanner and analysis differences in future multisite studies.

software_tool.answer: Custom mmVAE implementation in Python 3.7; Adam optimizer

response_variable.answer: Regional gray matter volumes (66 cortical ROIs + 24 subcortical ROIs, ICV-normalized); Regional amyloid FBP SUVR (66 cortical + 24 subcortical ROIs); Regional tau FTP SUVR (66 cortical + 24 subcortical ROIs)

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex were used as conditioning covariates in the decoder to control for their effects on brain measures. Both covariates were one-hot encoded (age: 44 positions for ages 47-91 years; sex: 2 positions). The model learns to reconstruct brain data after accounting for age and sex effects, ensuring that deviations reflect disease pathology rather than normal covariate-related variations.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study addresses some aspects of nuisance structure but not comprehensively. Age and sex effects are handled through one-hot encoding conditioning in the decoder. Dataset-specific differences (scanner, FreeSurfer version) are addressed through transfer learning/fine-tuning. However, the study does not explicitly use site as a random effect or covariate within the model, despite using two different datasets. The authors acknowledge limitations related to scanner differences and FreeSurfer version differences but chose transfer learning over explicit harmonization methods like ComBat. Heteroscedasticity and other forms of nuisance structure are not explicitly addressed in the model architecture.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We conditioned our proposed mmVAE on the age and sex of patients, to ensure that the deviations in regional brain volumes reflect only disease pathology and not deviations due to effects of covariates... For replication in the Knight ADRC dataset, mmVAE pretrained on ADNI-CU-train underwent fine-tuning on ADRC-CU-tl through transfer learning... These differences may introduce variability, particularly in more granular MRI volumetric measures, which could add noise to the normative model and potentially affect the robustness of our results. Although we fine-tuned our pre-trained normative model on the replication cohort to address dataset-specific biases... future multisite studies could further mitigate issues due to scanner and analysis differences using harmonization methods such as COMBAT.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Supplementary Methods SM4.3 (lines 52-54); Main text Section 2.5.1 (lines 123-124); Discussion Section 4.4 (lines 457-458)

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study uses a holdout validation set from the same dataset (ADNI-CU-holdout, n=65; ADRC-CU-holdout, n=45) that was split from the same cohort used for training. These validation sets are used to standardize/normalize deviations by calculating mean and variance independently for each region. This represents within-domain non-independent validation as the data comes from the same study population and acquisition protocol as the training set, though the specific individuals are different.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The ADNI-CU group was further divided into a training set for model training (ADNI-CU-train; n = 326), a holdout validation set (ADNI-CU-holdout; n = 65), and a test set (ADNI-CU-test; n = 43) at a ratio of 75:15:10... The validation set was used to standardize deviations of ADNI-ADS and calculate Z-scores relative to ADNI-CU... We utilized the mean and variance (calculated independently for each region) from ADNI-CU-holdout to normalize regional deviations in the ADNI-ADS cohort across each modality.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study includes a test set (ADNI-CU-test, n=43; ADRC-CU-test, n=31) from the same datasets that serves as a baseline control group for statistical comparisons with disease groups. However, the paper does not explicitly report standard normative model validation metrics (e.g., explained variance, MSLL, Pearson correlation, skewness, kurtosis of z-scores) on these independent healthy control test sets. The test sets are primarily used for group comparisons rather than explicit validation of normative model performance. Thus, while independent same-domain data exists, its use for explicit normative model validation is unclear or incomplete.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: The test sets served as a baseline control group to compare statistics of ADS individuals against amyloid-negative CU participants... We examined the magnitude of abnormal deviations in each region between amyloid negative CU individuals (CU-test; Section 2.1) and clinical groups along the ADS

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study performs explicit cross-dataset validation using a different-domain approach. The normative model is first developed on ADNI (discovery dataset) and then validated on the completely independent Knight ADRC dataset (replication dataset). The ADRC dataset differs from ADNI in multiple aspects: different recruitment site, different MRI scanners, different FreeSurfer version (5.3 vs 6.0), different demographic characteristics, and different disease severity distributions. The model undergoes transfer learning/fine-tuning on ADRC-CU-tl (n=225) to adapt to domain shift, and results are replicated showing similar patterns of heterogeneity, regional abnormal deviations, DSI associations with cognition and progression, validating the generalizability of findings across domains.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: We constructed a discovery dataset consisting of individuals from ADNI and a replication dataset consisting of individuals from the Charles F. and Joanne Knight ADRC dataset at Washington University in St. Louis... For replication in the Knight ADRC dataset, mmVAE pretrained on ADNI-CU-train underwent fine-tuning on ADRC-CU-tl through transfer learning... Our observations were reproducible in both the discovery and replication datasets, which demonstrated the generalizability of our scientific findings... We found a notable similarity between the effect size maps estimated in ADRC-ADS and in ADNI-ADS

clinical_dataset.answer: ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative) for discovery; Knight ADRC (Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center) for replication

diseases_studied.answer: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) spectrum: Preclinical AD (CDR=0, amyloid positive); Very mild dementia (CDR=0.5); Mild or more severe dementia (CDR≥1)

clinical_groups_n.answer: ADNI-ADS: CDR=0 (preclinical AD): 121; CDR=0.5: 80; CDR≥1: 30; Total: 231. ADRC-ADS: CDR=0: 98; CDR=0.5: 24; CDR≥1: 7; Total: 129

clinical_groups_age.answer: ADNI-ADS: mean 73.6 ± 6.9 years; ADRC-ADS: mean 71.5 ± 8.3 years

deviation_metric.answer: Z-score deviations: Regional Z-scores below -1.96 (bottom 2.5%) for MRI gray matter volumes indicating atrophy; Regional Z-scores above 1.96 (top 2.5%) for amyloid-FBP and tau-FTP SUVR indicating pathological accumulation. Binary thresholded abnormality maps created for each modality. Disease Severity Index (DSI) calculated separately for each modality (DSI_mri, DSI_amyloid, DSI_tau) and aggregated across all modalities (DSI_all) by computing inner product between binary abnormality map and regional deviation vector, normalized by total number of regions.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons: Cohen's d effect size for pairwise group differences between amyloid-negative CU and each CDR group, separately for each modality, with FDR correction. Intra-group heterogeneity: Hamming distance to measure dissimilarity in binary abnormality maps between every pair of individuals, visualized using kernel density estimation (KDE) plots. DSI-cognition associations: Linear regression adjusted for age and sex to examine associations between DSI values and neuropsychological composites (memory, executive functioning, language); Pearson correlation coefficients; Steiger's Z-test to compare correlations between DSI and classical ATN markers. DSI-progression associations: Survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier plots, log-rank tests) examining relationship between DSI_all quartiles and progression from CDR<1 to CDR≥1, adjusted for age and sex; FDR-corrected post-hoc comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study demonstrated heterogeneous patterns of abnormal deviations in gray matter volume, amyloid, and tau deposition across AD patients, with higher within-group heterogeneity at more severe dementia stages; the developed DSI metric showed significant associations with cognitive performance and increased risk of disease progression, with findings replicated across two independent datasets.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Regional analysis revealed that mild or more severe dementia showed pronounced atrophy in 56 (ADNI) and 50 (ADRC) regions, primarily in temporal, parietal, and hippocampal areas, while elevated amyloid burden was observed in 84-85 (ADNI) and 81-82 (ADRC) regions across all CDR groups, and increased tau deposition in 80 (ADNI) and 74 (ADRC) regions for severe cases. Proportion of abnormal deviations in hippocampus reached 47% in mild/severe dementia vs 3% in controls for MRI, while precuneus/frontal regions showed 100% vs 5% for amyloid in severe dementia vs controls. Hamming distance analysis demonstrated significantly higher within-group heterogeneity at progressive dementia stages (median hamming_all: mild/severe=62, very mild=56, preclinical=47, CU=5 for ADNI), with MRI showing highest spatial heterogeneity. DSI_all increased across dementia stages (ADNI: CDR≥1 mean=1.8, CDR=0.5 mean=1.1, CDR=0 mean=0.45, CU mean=0.06) with statistically significant pairwise differences except between very mild and severe groups. DSI_all showed strong negative correlations with cognitive performance in both cohorts (ADNI: memory r=-0.62, executive r=-0.54, language r=-0.47; ADRC: memory r=-0.68, executive r=-0.56, language r=-0.41, all p<0.001), outperforming modality-specific DSI measures. Survival analysis revealed higher DSI_all quartiles (q3 and q4) associated with significantly increased risk of progression to CDR≥1 compared to lower quartiles (p<0.001 for q4 vs q1 in both cohorts). Results were reproducible across ADNI and ADRC datasets, demonstrating generalizability despite demographic and technical differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Cross-sectional design limits ability to distinguish disease stages from subtypes and characterize progression over time; demographic differences between ADNI and ADRC cohorts (age, sex distribution) may affect generalization; both datasets from North America only, not representative of general population; different FreeSurfer versions (v6.0 for ADNI, v5.3 for ADRC) and different MRI scanners may introduce variability in volumetric measures; cerebrovascular disease burden, an important AD co-pathology, was not included in the ATN framework though the mmVAE framework is flexible enough to incorporate additional modalities; transfer learning partially addresses domain shifts but cannot fully account for demographic variations; future studies should incorporate longitudinal data, more diverse geographical populations, harmonization methods like ComBat, and vascular burden biomarkers.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study introduces DSI_all as a personalized metric of brain health that aggregates spatial extent and magnitude of regional abnormal deviations across multiple modalities (MRI, amyloid, tau), rather than relying on group-average relationships. DSI_all can potentially assist in clinical decision making and monitor patient response to FDA-approved anti-amyloid treatments (aducanumab, lecanemab). The multimodal mmVAE framework is flexible and can incorporate additional input modalities including vascular burden biomarkers (white matter hyperintensities, arterial spin labeling measures, diffusion tensor imaging metrics). Results challenge the validity of a 'typical AD' patient assumption common in case-control studies, showing partial overlap between patients with distinct regional patterns of abnormality. The study demonstrates that MRI shows highest within-group spatial heterogeneity, followed by tau and amyloid, consistent with prior subtyping studies showing more MRI/tau-driven subtypes than amyloid-driven ones. Code for the project will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

general_notes.general_notes: This study represents a comprehensive application of deep learning-based multimodal normative modeling to AD heterogeneity using ATN imaging biomarkers. The mmVAE architecture uses Product-of-Experts (POE) approach to combine modality-specific encoders into a shared latent space, with separate decoders for reconstruction. Model hyperparameters: epochs=500, learning rate=10^-5, batch size=256, latent dimension=64, with 4 fully connected layers (512-256-128-64 for encoders, reverse for decoders). Only Florbetapir (FBP) tracer data was included for both ADNI and ADRC to avoid harmonization issues with multiple tracers. Amyloid positivity cutoffs: ADNI used meta-ROI SUVR>1.11, ADRC used SUVR>1.24, both converted to Centiloid units. Tau index calculated as mean SUVR of four early-accumulation regions (entorhinal cortex, amygdala, lateral occipital cortex, inferior temporal cortex). Neuropsychological composites differed slightly between ADNI and ADRC due to test availability but covered same domains (memory, executive functioning, language). Longitudinal follow-up data available for 175 ADNI-ADS and 85 ADRC-ADS individuals with baseline CDR<1. ADNI showed higher overall pathology than ADRC even within similar CDR groups, likely due to ADNI's focus on later disease stages vs ADRC's preclinical focus with family history. Data availability: ADNI data publicly available through ADNI Data Sharing Committee; ADRC data available through data request form. Funding: NIH R01-AG067103, multiple NIH grants for computing facilities and data collection. The study is supported by extensive supplementary materials including detailed methods, model architecture diagrams, additional analyses on modality-specific DSI measures, case studies examining inter-patient variability, and multiple supplementary tables and figures.
